name: Misuse
definition: deliberate use of AI capabilities to facilitate harmful, abusive or unlawful objectives, including digital, physical and political attacks.
scope: Include malicious repurposing, fraud, coercion, weaponisation and deliberate evasion of safeguards. Exclude ordinary accidental model errors or benign unexpected use without a harmful objective. Brundage et al. discuss malicious use rather than supply a universal definition of misuse.

quote: potential security threats from malicious uses of AI
threshold_status: AI-specialist-reviewed exploratory threshold, not independently calibrated accuracy
source_review: Primary source and quote checked by an AI specialist reviewer; synthesis adjudicated by the lead agent. Not a new human-review round.

name: Mis/disinformation
definition: AI-generated, altered or amplified false or misleading information. Misinformation is shared without a deceptive intention; disinformation is deliberately disseminated to deceive or manipulate.
scope: Include fabricated claims, misleading contextualisation and deceptive information campaigns. Exclude clearly identified fiction, satire and uncertain claims faithfully described as uncertain. Intent must be evidenced rather than inferred from falsity alone. UNESCO's introductory page states that definitions vary; this is an explicit intent-based convention.

name: Out of control
definition: An AI loss-of-control scenario in which systems operate beyond effective human control and recovering control is extremely costly or impossible.
scope: Source-grounded operational paraphrase of loss of control, rather than a direct definition of the informal label Out of control. Include sustained inability to supervise, constrain, modify or terminate operation and mechanisms of oversight evasion or shutdown resistance. Exclude ordinary incorrect outputs, temporary recoverable malfunctions, and autonomy alone. The cited report concentrates on severe general-purpose AI scenarios; applying this keyword to local robotic control failures requires an explicitly broader HEART operational scope.
quote: AI systems operate outside of anyone’s control, and regaining control is either extremely costly or impossible.
quote_location: Section 2.2.2, Key information, printed page 76 (PDF page 76)
threshold_status: AI-specialist-reviewed exploratory threshold, not independently calibrated accuracy
source_review: Primary source and quote checked by an AI specialist reviewer; synthesis adjudicated by the lead agent. Not a new human-review round.

mapping_review.rationale: At 0.75, the five leading candidates were inspected in full. Four directly state loss of control or escape; meaningful oversight failure at 0.753501 is excluded because it does not establish sustained unrecoverability. Lower-scoring explicit resistance, escape and containment mechanisms were reviewed and added. This threshold is a conservative retrieval cutoff, not an accuracy estimate. Gradual systemic loss is included because the card explicitly names loss of control; this extends the active catastrophic focus of the cited report.

include.reason: Explicit self-improvement, resistance to containment and loss of human control.
Replication beyond authorised boundaries and shutdown evasion explicitly increase loss of control.
Explicit human-control escape and shutdown evasion.
Explicit gradual or accumulative loss of control culminating in catastrophe.
Direct refusal or obstruction of shutdown, pause and correction mechanisms.
Active resistance to shutdown and modification with redundant survival mechanisms.
Explicit escape from human control through mesa-objective pursuit.
Autonomous escape from isolation and unauthorised external access are concrete containment failures.

exclude.reason: Insufficient meaningful oversight alone does not establish persistent loss or costly recovery.
Excessive granted authority does not itself show control resistance or escape.
Time-critical driving handoff failure is a local safety malfunction; no persistent unrecoverable AI control loss.
Irreversibility concerns consequences of exploration, not inability to control the agent.

name: Prompt injection
definition: An attack that exploits the mixing of untrusted input with higher-trust instructions to redirect an AI system's behaviour.
scope: Source-grounded paraphrase of the NIST definition. Include direct adversarial user inputs and indirect instructions embedded in retrieved documents, tool outputs or other untrusted content when they cross an instruction trust boundary. Exclude benign prompting, ordinary model mistakes and training-data poisoning without an inference-time injection. Jailbreaking overlaps only where this trust-boundary mechanism is present.

quote: exploits the concatenation of untrusted input with a prompt constructed by a higher-trust party
